text:
sarah: heads-up — we're seeing repeated SQS message failures in prod because the combined trace header payload is > 256KB for some long-running requests. failures show up as `InvalidMessageContents` from the queue.
chris: huh. are those full span dumps getting attached to the message? I thought we only passed a tiny tracecontext + baggage keys.
sarah: that's the problem — our gateway currently serializes a `spans` array for the request when it crosses into async mode (we did that for replayability). for some large fanout jobs it's huge.
devon: two quick ideas — 1) shrink the on-wire carrier to a pointer (trace-id + minimal metadata) and store full spans in short-lived trace-store; 2) gzip + base64 the header and Mark it as compressed.
jen: gzip helps but SQS header size limit still applies — we hit broker size limits, not message body. also some consumers expect plain headers (older workers).
chris: what if we invert: send a tiny header: `X-RW-TraceRef: v1;id=...;hint=store:shardA:expires=30m` then exporters can fetch detail from internal trace-store over auth when they need full span payload. keeps queues light.
sarah: that avoids long headers but adds a dependency at consumer time. if consumer crashes before fetch we lose rich spans — but we still have minimal trace context for correlation.
devon: we could make fetch lazy and best-effort — i.e., workers correlate with trace-id and only call trace-store for detailed timeline during postmortem or sampling. runtime fast-path doesn't block on it.
jen: operationally, we need retention semantics for those short-lived stored spans. suggest 30m default with option to persist longer on explicit `store=true` provenance. also need E2E auth: tokens scoped to that request id.
sarah: agree. security note: stored spans may contain PII (prompt text etc). we must strip or redact sensitive attrs before putting into trace-store. add a transform step in gateway.
chris: also think about sampling: only store full payloads for 1% by default or whenever error flags set. otherwise carry only minimal trace context and aggregated metrics.
jen: UX question for console: in traces view, when a trace has a remote pointer we should show a small "full spans available" badge and lazy-load details. keeps dashboard snappy.
devon: implementation sketch: 
```
# header we send on queue
X-RW-TraceRef: v1;tid=ae3f...;short=1;st=2024-11-06T15:10:00Z;shard=s-17;sig=HMAC...
```
consumer flow: read header -> attach minimal span -> async fetch optional `GET /internal/traces/{shard}/{tid}?sig=...` -> merge if available.
```
# gateway transform config
REDWOOD_TRACE_STORE_RETENTION=30m
REDWOOD_TRACE_STORE_SAMPLING=0.01
REDWOOD_TRACE_REDACT_RULES=prompt,text,credit_card
```
chris: we also need backwards compatibility mode toggles. flag rollout via console so we can turn pointer-mode off for certain tenants.
sarah: can someone prototype a PoC? I'll open a design doc after this thread. devon — can you try a small prototype that stores to S3-like object store with temp creds and returns the header pointer?
devon: yep, I'll hack a POC this week. plan: gateway writes gzipped ndjson to s3/trace-store/{shard}/{tid}.gz with short TTL object lifecycle. consumer will have a simple fetcher lib.
otel-bot: (system) sampled traces currently forwarded to jaeger exporter; adding trace-store will not change jaeger export for now.
jen: one more thing — ensure our exporter telemetry marks whether trace detail was inline vs pointer vs missing. helps debug pipeline leaks.
sarah: good call. thanks all — i'll capture outcomes and proposed retention/sampling defaults in the doc.
chris: :thumbsup:
devon: I'll post the POC link when ready.
